content.text: The verifier is right — my first read was correct and my "repair" over-reached. § 12.4 is a non-compete, not a personnel non-solicit, so it belongs to an exclusivity/non-compete rule, not NOSOLICIT. Reverting to compliant with no redline.

input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Exhaustive searches for "solicit", "induce", "hire", "employ", "recruit", "poach", "staff", and "personnel", plus a full section-outline review, find no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binding Customer anywhere in the Agreement. § 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer has made no no-hire commitment and expressly preserves Customer's right to hire any person responding to general recruitment; § 30.1 is a standard independent-contractor clause imposing no personnel restriction. This matches the preferred position of no non-solicit on Customer, so no redline is required. The deterministic duration and general-solicitation-carve-out checks are inapplicable because there is no non-solicit obligation to measure. § 12.4 (a twenty-four-month general non-compete on competing products or services) restricts Customer but says nothing about soliciting, hiring, or engaging personnel; it is out of scope here and should be raised under the exclusivity/non-compete rule.
